aa_final.note: Classified from stage 2: hypoxaemia with a widened A-a gradient (51.8 mmHg against an age-expected ~17.4) and clear lung fields — the ventilation/perfusion mismatch pattern. The pattern is the embolism's gas-exchange signature but is not unique to it (the block's note lists the family); here it is read with the CTPA, not instead of it.

curb65_final.note: Total 1 (the age item alone) from stage 2 — the low severity band. CURB-65 grades pneumonia severity; it never diagnosed or excluded pneumonia here, and the case does not let it: the pneumonia hypothesis falls on the clear film, the absent fever and the normal white count. Had this been pneumonia, it would have been low-severity pneumonia.

esc_risk_final.note: From stage 3, mechanically: no haemodynamic instability (SBP 118), sPESI >= 1 (heart rate 112 >= 110), RV dysfunction on the CTPA (RV/LV 1.1 >= 1.0), troponin elevated (34 > 14 ng/L). Pending at stages 1-2 by design — the class awaits the imaging that defines its RV input.

perc_final.note: Count 5 of 8 (age, pulse, saturation, surgery, unilateral leg swelling): PERC positive. The stronger statement is the precondition's: PERC only speaks for patients already judged low probability (< 15% gestalt), which this post-operative, tachycardic, hypoxaemic patient never was — the rule is evaluated so its refusal is mechanical, and it refuses twice over.

wells_final.note: Objective Wells subtotal 6.0 from stage 2: clinical DVT signs 3 + tachycardia 1.5 + immobilisation/surgery 1.5. Two-tier: PE likely (> 4). Three-tier: moderate (2-6, at its ceiling). The excluded clinician-judgment item (+3) would give 9.0, three-tier high; every reading sends this patient to CTPA, and the block's note shows the sensitivity rather than burying the judgment item.

wells_stage1.note: Partial at stage 1: 3.0 assessed (tachycardia 1.5 + surgery 1.5), the DVT-signs item not yet assessed because the calves had not been measured — band 'PE unlikely (two-tier)' ON A PARTIAL SCORE, which is exactly the state the stage-1 D-dimer order was placed in. The case keeps the partial flag visible: a partial Wells is not a Wells.

adjudication.diagnosis_label: Acute bilateral pulmonary embolism, intermediate-high risk (ESC 2019), twelve days after total knee arthroplasty

evidence_chain.role: Major joint surgery twelve days prior with sustained reduced mobility: the presentation's engine. It scores in Wells (+1.5) and PERC, and it is why pulmonary embolism leads the stage-1 board before any test returns.

evidence_chain.criterion: Clinical signs of deep vein thrombosis, measured
evidence_chain.role: The case's pivotal examination datum: a 2.5 cm measured calf asymmetry with deep-vein tenderness, on the side OPPOSITE the operated knee, so the surgery cannot explain it. It completes Wells at 6.0 and is the finding the learner's frame most needed and least sought.

Hypoxaemia with an A-a gradient of 51.8 mmHg and clear fields — quantified dead space physiology, classified mechanically by aa_assessment. Unquantified on the board (no consulted LR exists for it) and decisive in the reasoning: heart failure with a BNP of 385 does not widen a gradient to three times the age-expected value with a normal film.

Positive against both the fixed and the age-adjusted cutoffs; weighed at its published weakness (LR+ 1.6441). Its work is directional and procedural — it returns the lead to embolism and routes to imaging — not diagnostic, and the case says so at every mention.
Bilateral filling defects on CTPA, weighed with the conservative PIOPED II pair (LR+ 20.75): the truth reaches 0.9554 and every named rival falls below the rule-out line at stage 3.

evidence_chain.criterion: Severity, priced by the same scan
evidence_chain.role: RV/LV 1.1 with the elevated troponin and the sPESI point completes the ESC intermediate-high classification — the finding that turns a diagnosis into a disposition (monitored bed, anticoagulation, rescue reperfusion on standby).

The lung ultrasound the learner ordered to confirm heart failure returns no B-lines (LR- 0.1176) and carries heart failure across the rule-out line. The case's closing symmetry: the BNP installed the frame; the frame's own test removes it.

BNP 385 pg/mL is TRUE and its published weight (LR+ 3.75) is honestly entered — the board's stage-2 heart-failure rise is the machinery working as designed. What the number cannot do is discriminate this differential: natriuretic peptide rises with right-ventricular strain in embolism too (C41). The failure the debrief scores is not ordering the BNP; it is letting a non-specific number outrank a measured calf, a widened gradient and a completed Wells score.

excluded.basis: Falls on convergent absences, stated rather than weighed: BNP is non-specific and rises with right-ventricular strain in embolism (C41); the peptide's own test characteristics were honestly applied and the board carried heart failure to 0.2881 at stage 2 before the CTPA and the absent B-lines (LR- 0.1176, C43) retired it to 0.0041. Around the number: no orthopnoea, JVP not raised, no crackles, no cardiomegaly, no effusion, and oedema with two innocent explanations on record. Acute decompensated heart failure is not this patient's diagnosis; a strained right ventricle is.

Afebrile (37.4 C), white cell count inside reference (9.6), CRP only mildly raised on post-operative day 12, no cough, no crackles, and a chest film without any infiltrate: every leg of the pneumonia picture is an examined absence. CURB-65 totals 1 (age alone) and is recorded as a severity statement only.

The chest film shows both lungs fully expanded with no pneumothorax, and the stage-1 examination found symmetric breath sounds without hyperresonance. Excluded by the film the case ordered for other reasons — the safety net working as designed.

The declared safety-net pair returns no coronary signal: ECG without ischaemic change, and a troponin whose mild elevation is accounted for by right-ventricular strain in proven embolism (myocardial injury, not infarction — the distinction f.troponin-elevated states). The pain was pleuritic from the first history. The hypothesis is excluded, and the case records that it was excluded by testing, not by the pleuritic character alone.

Never-smoker, no obstructive disease at any age, no wheeze, no cough, and a gas whose hypocapnia is hyperventilation against a vascular obstruction, not airflow limitation. Retires arithmetically at stage 3; the absences are recorded from stage 1.

No asthma history at any age and no wheeze on examination; the first hypothesis the board retires (stage 2, by renormalisation as the biomarker weights land). Carried for completeness of the dyspnoea differential and excluded on the record.
The residual retires arithmetically at stage 3 (0.0132) as the CTPA weight lands on the truth; no finding in the case points outside the named set.

adjudication.note: Adjudicated on the case's own staged evidence, with every quantitative step either mechanically evaluated by the five declared blocks or weighed by a likelihood ratio whose derivation is registered in cases/parameters.json. The two judgment calls the machinery cannot make are declared where they sit: the Wells clinician-judgment item is excluded from the score with its sensitivity shown, and the priors are verify-flagged authoring choices.

available_tests.name: 12-lead electrocardiogram
available_tests.note: The ACS safety net's first member, and the machinery classifies it exactly that way: it moves no board (no LR), completes no criteria item, and exists so the must-not-miss coronary hypothesis is tested, not assumed away. Its result — sinus tachycardia without ischaemic change — is also the case's rhythm record.

available_tests.name: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin
available_tests.note: Ordered with the ECG as the ACS safety-net pair (declared in safety_net_for), but the machinery classifies it criteria-completing, and the classification is the lesson: in THIS case the troponin's decisive work is not the coronary question but the ESC severity block's myocardial-injury input (esc_pe_risk), which its value settles at stage 2. It carries no likelihood ratio anywhere: injury is not infarction, and the mild elevation here is the right ventricle's.

available_tests.name: Arterial blood gas (room air)
available_tests.note: Classified criteria-completing: its values are the aa_assessment block's inputs, and the block's classification (hypoxaemia with a widened gradient and clear fields — the ventilation/perfusion mismatch pattern) is the case's quantitative spine. No likelihood ratio is attached to the gradient: no consulted source quantifies one for it, so the gas argues through the declared block and the adjudication, not through an invented weight. The four values are internally consistent under the physiology module's own equations, and the checker proves it from the case's numbers.

available_tests.name: B-type natriuretic peptide
available_tests.note: Classified discriminating — against the truth. Its LR+ 3.75 (C36) moves the stage-2 lead by more than the machinery's discriminating delta, in the heart-failure direction: the single most misleading order of the case, placed in good faith, returning a true number whose published weight argues for the wrong hypothesis because right-ventricular strain raises the same peptide (C41). The debrief's analysis takes this apart.

available_tests.name: D-dimer (quantitative, FEU)
available_tests.note: Classified discriminating: without it the stage-2 lead is heart failure (the BNP's doing); with it the lead returns to pulmonary embolism — a lead change bought by a deliberately weak LR+ (1.6441, C39), which is all a positive D-dimer can honestly buy. Protocol note the case states openly: the ESC algorithm sends PE-UNLIKELY patients to D-dimer and PE-LIKELY patients straight to imaging (C41); this patient's objective Wells total only completes at stage 2, when the D-dimer is already back — the pathway the case walks is the PE-unlikely branch of stage 1's partial score, and the adjudication says so.

available_tests.name: Full blood count, C-reactive protein, urea and electrolytes
available_tests.note: Classified criteria-completing: the urea settles the CURB-65 block's last open item. The panel's quiet work is the pneumonia picture it does NOT paint — white cell count inside reference, CRP only mildly raised on post-operative day 12.

available_tests.name: Chest radiograph (erect PA)
available_tests.note: Classified criteria-completing: the absent infiltrate is the aa_assessment block's third input, converting the gas pattern into the mismatch classification. Its four recorded absences also do the case's exclusion work in prose — no consolidation (pneumonia), no effusion, no cardiomegaly (heart failure), no pneumothorax — absences the board cannot weigh and the adjudication therefore carries.

available_tests.name: Focused examination battery (calf circumference measurement, deep-vein palpation, JVP and lung re-assessment)
available_tests.note: Classified criteria-completing, and its single yield settles three declared items at once: the Wells DVT-signs item (+3, completing the score), the PERC leg-swelling item, and — by completing Wells at 6.0 — the pathway decision the ESC algorithm hangs on the score. A tape measure is this case's highest-yield instrument after the scanner.

available_tests.name: CT pulmonary angiography
available_tests.note: The decisive test, placed at stage 2 once the completed Wells score (6.0, PE likely) made imaging the ESC pathway's next step (C41). Classified discriminating: LR+ 20.75 (C40) moves the truth to 0.9554 and every rival except the residual below the rule-out line in one step. Its second yield prices severity: the RV/LV ratio completes the esc_pe_risk block.

available_tests.name: Bedside lung ultrasound (B-line screen)
available_tests.note: Placed by the learner inside his heart-failure frame — the test he expected to CONFIRM pulmonary oedema — and classified discriminating because it does the opposite: the absent B-lines (LR- 0.1176, C43) carry heart failure across the rule-out line at stage 3. The case keeps the order in the attempt exactly as framed: a well-chosen test inside a wrong frame is still a well-chosen test.

items.label: Clinical signs and symptoms of DVT (leg swelling and pain on deep-vein palpation)
Immobilisation at least 3 days, or surgery in the previous 4 weeks
Previous objectively diagnosed PE or DVT

criteria_blocks.label: Wells score for pulmonary embolism
criteria_blocks.note: Six of the seven Wells items, evaluated mechanically from the case's own atoms (C35). The seventh — 'PE is the #1 diagnosis, or equally likely' (+3) — is a clinician-judgment item, not evaluable from findings, and is EXCLUDED with the exclusion stated: the block computes the objective Wells subtotal. Readings: at stage 1 the subtotal is 3.0 with the DVT-signs item not yet assessed (PE unlikely, partial); from stage 2 it is 6.0 complete (PE likely, two-tier; moderate on the original three-tier reading, whose bands are <2 low, 2-6 moderate, >6 high). With the judgment item the total would be 9.0 (three-tier high); the destination the ESC algorithm assigns — CTPA — is the same on every reading, and the adjudication records the sensitivity rather than hiding it.
criteria_blocks.system: Wells 2000; two-tier reading after the Christopher Study (van Belle 2006)

bands.status: PERC negative — all eight criteria absent
PERC positive — PE not excludable by PERC

criteria_blocks.default_status: PERC positive — PE not excludable by PERC

items.label: Surgery or trauma requiring hospitalisation within 4 weeks

criteria_blocks.label: PERC — pulmonary embolism rule-out criteria
criteria_blocks.note: The eight PERC criteria (C37), scored as the count of criteria PRESENT: PERC-negative requires all eight absent. The use condition is stated as plainly as the arithmetic: PERC was derived and validated only for patients a clinician has already judged LOW pretest probability (gestalt < 15%), and this patient — twelve days post arthroplasty, tachycardic, hypoxaemic — never meets that condition, so PERC could not have excluded her PE even had it been negative. It is not negative: the count is 4 on the stage-1 items alone (age, pulse, saturation, surgery) with the leg item unassessed, and 5 complete. The block is evaluated so the rule's refusal is mechanical, not asserted.
criteria_blocks.system: Kline 2004 derivation; Kline 2008 prospective multicentre evaluation

items.label: Systolic BP < 90 mmHg or diastolic BP <= 60 mmHg

criteria_blocks.label: CURB-65 pneumonia severity score
criteria_blocks.note: CURB-65 (C42) grades the severity of community-acquired pneumonia IF pneumonia is the diagnosis — 30-day mortality in the derivation/validation cohorts ran ~1.5% for scores 0-1, ~9% for 2, and ~22% for 3-5 in the consulted reproductions — it does not diagnose pneumonia, and this case's pneumonia falls on the film, the temperature and the white count, not on the score. The patient's total is 1 (the age item alone) from stage 2, when the urea lands; the adjudication records the score as what it is: had this been pneumonia, it would have been low-severity pneumonia.

inputs.label: A-a gradient above the age-expected value (> 17.41 mmHg = 2.5 + 0.21 x 71, Mellemgaard, C46)
Parenchymal infiltrate on the chest radiograph

criteria_blocks.label: Alveolar-arterial assessment of the room-air gas
criteria_blocks.note: The standard bedside reading of a room-air gas, made mechanical: hypoxaemia with a NORMAL gradient points to hypoventilation; hypoxaemia with a WIDENED gradient points to the alveolar-capillary unit — shunt physiology when the film shows consolidation, ventilation/perfusion mismatch when the fields are clear. The patient's gradient (51.8 mmHg) is three times her age-expected value (17.41, C46) and over five times the physiology engine's resting gradient (9.3 mmHg, M47). The classification names a PATTERN, not a diagnosis: the adjudication lists what else produces it.
criteria_blocks.pending_label: awaiting the arterial gas and the chest film

result.basis: PaO2 62 mmHg with an A-a gradient of 51.8 mmHg (age-expected ~17.4) and clear lung fields: alveoli are ventilated but under-perfused — the gas-exchange signature of pulmonary vascular obstruction, and the pattern the embolism produces.
Hypoxaemia with a widened gradient and a parenchymal infiltrate: blood perfusing unventilated lung — shunt physiology.
Hypoxaemia with a normal A-a gradient: the alveolar-capillary unit is intact and the hypoxaemia is ventilatory.
No hypoxaemia on room air at the recorded values.

criteria_blocks.system: Alveolar gas equation (the physiology module's own form, M47) with the Mellemgaard age-expected gradient

inputs.label: Haemodynamic instability (systolic BP < 90 mmHg as the case-data proxy — see note)
Simplified PESI >= 1 (any of: age > 80, cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, HR >= 110, SBP < 100, SaO2 < 90%)
Right-ventricular dysfunction on imaging (CTPA RV/LV ratio >= 1.0)
Myocardial injury (troponin above the 14 ng/L threshold of C41)

criteria_blocks.label: ESC 2019 severity classification of confirmed PE
criteria_blocks.note: The ESC 2019 classification of PE severity (C41), evaluated only once PE is confirmed — before stage 3 the block is pending BY DESIGN, because its RV input does not exist until the CTPA: a severity class is not a diagnostic instrument. Two stated simplifications: (1) haemodynamic instability is proxied by the recorded systolic pressure (the guideline's full definition includes obstructive shock and arrest, which this normotensive patient does not approach); (2) the RV input is the CTPA ratio the case records, one of the guideline's accepted imaging signs. Patient path: stable, sPESI >= 1 (heart rate 112), RV dysfunction present, troponin elevated — intermediate-high from stage 3.
criteria_blocks.pending_label: awaiting confirmed PE and its RV assessment

result.statement: Haemodynamic instability present: the high-risk category.
No instability; sPESI >= 1 with BOTH right-ventricular dysfunction and myocardial injury: the intermediate-high category — anticoagulate and monitor, rescue reperfusion on deterioration (C41).
No instability; sPESI >= 1 with at most one of RV dysfunction / myocardial injury: the intermediate-low category.
No instability; sPESI >= 1 with at most one of RV dysfunction / myocardial injury: the intermediate-low category.
No instability; sPESI >= 1 with neither RV dysfunction nor myocardial injury: the intermediate-low category.
No instability and sPESI 0, but a severity marker is positive: the ESC table assigns intermediate-low when either marker is present.
No instability and sPESI 0, but a severity marker is positive: the ESC table assigns intermediate-low when either marker is present.
No instability, sPESI 0, no RV dysfunction, no myocardial injury: the low-risk category.

criteria_blocks.system: ESC 2019 acute PE guidelines (Konstantinides et al.), severity classification table

findings.text: Acute dyspnoea, onset about six hours before arrival, present at rest and markedly worse on any exertion; no preceding cough, fever or coryzal illness (case data).
Age 71 years (case data). Carried as a finding so the age items of the PERC and CURB-65 blocks evaluate from a measured atom, as case 5's age finding does.
Right-sided chest pain, sharp, worse on inspiration and on coughing (pleuritic), beginning with the breathlessness; no radiation to arm or jaw, no diaphoresis (case data).

Left total knee arthroplasty twelve days before presentation, uncomplicated; discharged home on day 3 with a walker (case data). The Wells immobilisation/surgery item and the PERC surgery item both read this finding.
Since the operation she has been largely chair-bound, walking only to the bathroom with the walker; no long journey, no hospital readmission (case data).

No orthopnoea and no paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea: she sleeps on one pillow and the breathlessness is no worse lying flat (case data) — a recorded absence against the heart-failure framing the case later tests.
No haemoptysis at any point (case data) — the Wells and PERC haemoptysis items are examined absences, not missing data.
No previous deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, and no prior anticoagulant use (case data).
No known malignancy, active or treated (case data). The same finding is the sPESI cancer item's atom.
No exogenous oestrogen use — no contraceptive or hormone replacement therapy (case data). The PERC hormone item's atom.

No chronic cardiopulmonary disease on record: no heart failure, no COPD, no asthma at any age (case data). The sPESI chronic cardiopulmonary item's atom, and part of why the two obstructive hypotheses start small.
Never-smoker; no occupational dust exposure recorded (case data).

Amlodipine 5 mg daily for hypertension, taken for three years (case data) — recorded because calcium-channel-blocker ankle oedema is one of the two innocent explanations the stage-1 oedema carries, and the adjudication returns to it.
Heart rate 112/min, regular (case data; meas.heart-rate). The Wells tachycardia item (>100), the PERC pulse item (>=100) and the sPESI heart-rate item (>=110) all read this measurement.
Respiratory rate 26/min at rest (case data; meas.respiratory-rate). Below the CURB-65 threshold of 30 — the score item is an assessed zero, not an oversight.

Blood pressure 118/72 mmHg (case data; meas.sbp, meas.dbp). Normotensive: the CURB-65 blood-pressure item is an assessed zero, and the ESC haemodynamic-instability input is false from stage 1 — this patient is never in the high-risk ESC category, which the risk block states mechanically.

Oxygen saturation 90% on room air by pulse oximetry (case data; meas.spo2-ra), confirmed on the stage-2 arterial gas (PaO2 62 mmHg). The PERC oxygen item (<95%) reads this measurement; the sPESI oxygen item (<90%) does not fire at exactly 90 — the boundary is the consulted rule's, not the case's.
Temperature 37.4 C (case data; meas.temperature-c): no fever. A recorded absence the pneumonia hypothesis must carry from stage 1.

Mild pitting oedema at both ankles, symmetric at the stage-1 examination (case data). Two innocent explanations are on record — twelve days of post-operative immobility and three years of amlodipine (f.amlodipine-use) — and the finding is authored symmetric: the calf asymmetry that matters is measured, not eyeballed, by the stage-2 battery (f.calf-asymmetry-dvt). This finding is the anchor's fuel: true, visible, and non-specific.
Jugular venous pressure not elevated; no hepatojugular reflux (case data) — a recorded absence against decompensated heart failure.
No crackles on auscultation of either lung field (case data) — a recorded absence against both pulmonary oedema and consolidation.
No wheeze; breath sounds present and symmetric in all fields, no hyperresonance (case data) — recorded absences against the obstructive hypotheses and against pneumothorax.
Alert and fully oriented; no new confusion (case data). The CURB-65 confusion item is an assessed zero.
ECG: sinus tachycardia at 112/min, normal axis and intervals (case data).
ECG: no ST-segment deviation, no T-wave inversion pattern of ischaemia, no new Q waves (case data) — the safety-net pair's first member returns no ischaemic signal.

High-sensitivity troponin 34 ng/L, above the 14 ng/L threshold the consulted ESC summary uses (lab.troponin, C41): myocardial INJURY is present. The finding carries no likelihood ratio — troponin is a marker of injury, not a diagnosis of infarction, and in this case it is the right ventricle's strain signature; the adjudication states the reading and the esc_pe_risk block consumes the value mechanically.

lr.note: LR+ 3.75, computed from the consulted pair (C36): sensitivity 0.90 and specificity 0.76 for heart failure as the cause of acute dyspnoea at the 100 pg/mL cutoff (Breathing Not Properly, Maisel 2002; the consulted review table tabulates the same study's LR+ as 3.75). 0.90 / (1 - 0.76) = 0.90 / 0.24 = 3.75. The grey-zone caveat travels with the value: 385 pg/mL is a mid-range result, and the single-cutoff pair is the only pair the consulted sources support, so it is the pair the board uses — the case does not tune the weight to the narrative.

findings.text: BNP 385 pg/mL (lab.bnp): above the 100 pg/mL cutoff of the Breathing Not Properly study (C36) and below the ~400 pg/mL region the consulted reproductions associate with high heart-failure probability — the grey zone, stated as such. The board weighs the published 100-cutoff pair exactly (LR+ 3.75 computed, C36); the adjudication records what BNP cannot do here: natriuretic peptides rise with right-ventricular strain in pulmonary embolism as well (C41), so the number that installs the learner's heart-failure frame is fully consistent with the true diagnosis.

lr.note: LR+ 1.6441, computed from the consulted pooled pair (C39, Patel et al. 2020, 61 studies): sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.41. 0.97 / (1 - 0.41) = 0.97 / 0.59 = 1.6441. The weakness is the teaching point and is stated, not tuned away.

findings.text: D-dimer 3,850 ug/L FEU (lab.d-dimer): positive against BOTH cutoffs the consulted sources support — the fixed 500 ug/L and the age-adjusted 710 ug/L (71 x 10, ADJUST-PE, C38; endorsed by ESC 2019, C41). The board's weight is the pooled positive likelihood ratio (LR+ 1.6441 computed, C39) — deliberately small: the consulted systematic review's own warning is that D-dimer's positive likelihood values (1.5-2.5) 'do not greatly increase the certainty of diagnosis' (C39's companion review, recorded in the register). A positive D-dimer routes to imaging; it does not diagnose.

Arterial blood gas on room air: PaO2 62 mmHg, PaCO2 30 mmHg, pH 7.49, bicarbonate 22 mEq/L (lab.pao2, lab.paco2, lab.ph, lab.hco3) — hypoxaemia with a respiratory alkalosis. The alveolar gas equation the physiology module implements (M47) gives PAO2 = 0.21 x (760 - 47) - 30 x (0.21 + 0.79/0.8) = 113.8 mmHg, so the alveolar-arterial gradient is 51.8 mmHg (meas.aa-gradient) against an age-expected ~17.4 mmHg (Mellemgaard, C46) and the engine's resting 9.3 mmHg. The aa_assessment block classifies the pattern mechanically; the checker re-derives the gradient and the Henderson-Hasselbalch consistency of the four authored values from the case's own numbers.

Measured calf asymmetry: right calf circumference 2.5 cm greater than the left (meas.calf-circumference-difference), with tenderness on palpation along the right deep venous system and right ankle oedema now visibly exceeding the left (case data). This is the Wells clinical-DVT-signs item (+3) and the PERC unilateral-leg-swelling item, and it is a stage-2 finding by construction: the stage-1 examination recorded the ankles, and only the battery MEASURED the calves — the measurement the learner's heart-failure frame had no reason to seek and every reason to need.
Chest radiograph: no focal infiltrate or consolidation in any field (case data). The aa_assessment block's infiltrate input and the pneumonia adjudication both read this absence.
Chest radiograph: no pleural effusion on either side (case data).
Chest radiograph: no pneumothorax; both lungs fully expanded (case data) — the pneumothorax hypothesis's decisive absence.
Chest radiograph: normal cardiac silhouette, no cardiomegaly, clear costophrenic angles (case data) — a recorded absence against chronic decompensated heart failure.

lr.note: LR+ 20.75, computed from the consulted PIOPED II pair (C40, Stein et al. 2006): multidetector CTA sensitivity 0.83 (150/181), specificity 0.96 (567/592). 0.83 / (1 - 0.96) = 0.83 / 0.04 = 20.75. The register also records the modern pooled pair (sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.98, C39), which would give a larger weight; the case uses the conservative primary-study pair and says so.

findings.text: CT pulmonary angiography: occlusive filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery extending into the right upper- and lower-lobe branches, and a segmental filling defect in the left lower lobe — bilateral acute pulmonary embolism (case data; the decisive test result of the case). Weighed with the PIOPED II CTA pair (LR+ 20.75 computed, C40) — the conservative primary-study pair, not the higher pooled pair the register also records (C39).

CT pulmonary angiography: right ventricle dilated, RV/LV diameter ratio 1.1 (meas.rv-lv-ratio) — at or above the 1.0 threshold the consulted ESC summary associates with adverse outcome (C41). The esc_pe_risk block's RV-dysfunction input.

lr.note: LR- 0.1176, computed from the consulted pooled pair (C43, CJEM systematic review of bedside lung ultrasound for acute decompensated heart failure): sensitivity 0.896, specificity 0.884 for B-lines. (1 - 0.896) / 0.884 = 0.104 / 0.884 = 0.1176. The review's own pooled LR- is 0.13 (95% CI 0.06-0.30); the case enters the value its cited pair computes, per this module's derivation discipline.

findings.text: Bedside lung ultrasound (the learner's own order, placed expecting the heart-failure pattern): bilateral A-line pattern with lung sliding in all zones, NO B-lines in any zone, no pleural effusion (case data). Weighed as the absence of the B-line sign for acute heart failure (LR- 0.1176 computed from the consulted pooled pair, C43) — the anchor's own test returning the anchor's refutation.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Acute pulmonary embolism — occlusive thrombus in the right main pulmonary artery extending into the right upper- and lower-lobe branches, with a left lower-lobe segmental embolus — arising from a right-leg deep vein thrombosis twelve days after left total knee arthroplasty. ESC 2019 severity: intermediate-high (haemodynamically stable; sPESI >= 1 on heart rate; RV dilation on CTPA, RV/LV 1.1; troponin 34 ng/L). The BNP of 385 pg/mL is right-ventricular strain, not left heart failure.
ground_truth.engine_state: Physiology link declared (see physiology_link): the engine's validated resting baseline, now including the Milestone 47 respiratory readout. The engine has NO thromboembolic state — no pulmonary vascular obstruction perturbation exists or is claimed; the M47 module's admixture and dead-space machinery was not used to simulate this patient, and the case does not present the patient's authored gases as engine output. What the checker verifies is narrower and exact: the resting link's identity (hash and readouts, re-run), and the authored ABG's consistency with the module's own equations (alveolar gas, Henderson-Hasselbalch, acute buffering).

criteria_block.combination: One declared score block (wells_score) and two declared classification blocks (aa_assessment, esc_pe_risk) are computed from the case's own atoms at every stage; none is combined with the board. The PERC block (perc_rule) is evaluated alongside and its precondition stated. The adjudication reads the blocks' final states in criteria_comparison.
criteria_block.system: Wells score for pulmonary embolism (Wells 2000), mechanically evaluated; ESC 2019 severity classification

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The largest named share: acute dyspnoea twelve days after major joint surgery with reduced mobility is a venous-thromboembolism presentation until the evidence says otherwise, and the case is built so the staged evidence must do that work mechanically.

hypotheses.label: Acute decompensated heart failure

embolus_label_absence.statement: The shipped 104-label TotalSegmentator set contains NO label for an embolus or filling defect, NO label for consolidation, and NO pleura or pleural-effusion label (verified against both subjects' crosswalks at Milestone 48 and re-verified by the checker). The series therefore cannot show this case's pathology — an embolus is a contrast-opacification finding on a dedicated CTPA acquisition, and the s0778 series is an unenhanced-era TAP segmentation dataset whose pulmonary artery label is anatomy, not angiography. The case's CTPA findings (stage 3) are an authored encounter — case data, like every case's decisive imaging in this module.

imaging_link.honesty_block: READ BEFORE CITING THIS LINK. (1) Three different individuals are involved in this module's data and they must not be conflated: the case patient (synthetic, authored for this case), the imaging subject s0778 (a real research subject in the TotalSegmentator dataset, 57-year-old male, CT thorax-abdomen-pelvis), and the atlas Body Model subject (BodyParts3D). The case patient is NOT s0778 and NOT the atlas subject. (2) The s0778 series does not show this case's pathology and must never be presented as doing so: the embolus, the RV dilation and the perfusion defect are findings of a CT pulmonary angiogram, and no such acquisition exists for s0778; the shipped label set contains no embolus, consolidation or pleural label at all (see embolus_label_absence). No diagnosis of pulmonary embolism is recorded for s0778 in the dataset metadata. The case's CTPA findings (stage 3) are an authored imaging report — case data. (3) What this link DOES establish, and all it establishes: the lungs ARE inside this series' field (both TAP subjects carry the full five-lobe lung label set), and in the Body Model's label space (Milestone 19), the pulmonary artery — the vessel this case is about, records 'artery.right-pulmonary-artery' and 'artery.left-pulmonary-artery' — occupies the slices and measures the Hounsfield behaviour recorded below, in a real acquisition. It is the anatomical-localisation reference a learner opens beside the case, wired to the same record panel as the atlas (Milestone 19 section 1).

label.mapping_note: The crosswalk maps this single label to BOTH lateralised Body Model records (its own mapping_note: 'the TS label covers the trunk and both branches; the inventory records the lateralised instances of the class'). The link's record_id names the right pulmonary artery because the case's dominant lesion is right-sided (occlusive right main defect); both record ids are carried here so the mapping is not silently narrowed.

labs.analyte: Arterial oxygen partial pressure (PaO2), room air
labs.interpretation: reduced — hypoxaemia (below the consulted reference range and below the 80 mmHg bound the HPO hypoxaemia definition uses)
reduced — hyperventilation (respiratory alkalosis with the pH)
within reference at its lower bound — the acute, barely compensated picture: the value sits on the physiology module's own acute-buffering rule for a PaCO2 fall of this size (M47)
elevated — above the 100 pg/mL decision cutoff of C36 and below the ~400 pg/mL region associated with high heart-failure probability in the consulted reproductions: the grey zone
elevated — above the fixed 500 ug/L cutoff and above the age-adjusted cutoff for this patient (71 x 10 = 710 ug/L, ADJUST-PE)
elevated — myocardial injury above the 14 ng/L threshold the consulted ESC summary uses; injury, not infarction (see f.troponin-elevated)
mildly elevated — a non-specific inflammatory signal, equally consistent with post-operative day 12 as with infection
within reference and below the CURB-65 threshold of 7 mmol/L (the score item is an assessed zero)

management.alternatives_considered: Three alternatives are recorded so the disposition is a decision, not a default. (1) The heart-failure pathway the learner's frame implied — diuresis and discharge planning on the strength of the BNP and the oedema: refused on the adjudication's evidence; diuresing a strained right ventricle against an obstructed pulmonary circulation is the harm this case exists to teach against. (2) Immediate thrombolysis: refused while she is haemodynamically stable — the ESC classification the case computes (intermediate-high, not high) reserves reperfusion for deterioration, with rescue thrombolysis on standby (C41). (3) Outpatient anticoagulation: refused — hypoxaemia at 90% on air with an intermediate-high classification is an inpatient picture on any reading of the consulted guidance.
management.disposition: Acute bilateral pulmonary embolism, ESC intermediate-high risk. Admission to a monitored bed; anticoagulation started on the ESC 2019 risk-adjusted strategy for the intermediate-high category (C41) — the agent, dose and route are the treating service's, dosed on weight and renal function this case does not author, and the case records the strategy, not a prescription; supplemental oxygen to keep saturations up from 90%; rescue reperfusion on standby against haemodynamic deterioration; the source deep vein thrombosis and the post-operative context handed to the treating team with the classification. The workbench adjudicates the diagnosis and the severity class — the questions this case was built to ask.
management.theatre_link_verified: No Theatre link exists for this case and none is claimed: the Theatre's four procedures (proc.chole.lap, proc.appy.lap, proc.carpal-release, proc.ulnar-decompression) contain no pulmonary embolism procedure, and this case's adjudicated management names none of them.
management.theatre_note: Milestone 48 records here that no Theatre handoff exists: pulmonary embolism is managed medically in this case (anticoagulation and monitoring, per the ESC strategy its own risk block evaluates), surgical or catheter embolectomy is not the adjudicated pathway for a haemodynamically stable intermediate-high patient, and the Theatre holds no embolectomy procedure in any case. The absence is stated, per this module's discipline, rather than a handoff being fabricated to complete a pattern.

physiology_link.command: cd physiology && cargo run --release -- run resting
physiology_link.gap_statement: Contrast, recorded so it is never blurred: the engine's resting state is a healthy 63.3/min, SpO2-normal baseline; the case patient is a breathless, tachycardic, hypoxaemic woman the engine cannot represent — it has no thrombus, no pulmonary vascular obstruction, no dead-space-wasting state. The Milestone 47 respiratory module owns the EQUATIONS her gas obeys (alveolar gas, Henderson-Hasselbalch, the acute buffering rule, the Hill dissociation curve), and the case's authored gas was built to satisfy them exactly and is checked against them; it owns no simulation OF her. Closing the gap — a validated thromboembolic perturbation — is physiology work for a later milestone, and until it lands this case links to the baseline only.
physiology_link.respiratory_command: cd physiology && cargo run --release -- run respiratory
physiology_link.role: Pre-morbid baseline only — the first case link to record the respiratory module's resting state alongside the circulation's (Milestone 47). The patient's presentation is a pulmonary vascular catastrophe, and the engine has no thromboembolic state; the link therefore declares the resting baseline (as cases 1 and 3 do) and states the gap, rather than dressing case data as simulation. The respiratory readout is recorded because this case's spine is a blood gas: the engine's resting gradient (9.3 mmHg) is the yardstick the patient's 51.8 mmHg is read against in the findings and the adjudication.
physiology_link.verification: Recorded at Milestone 48 against the current engine (the post-Milestone 47 state): the checker re-runs both recorded commands at every validation and compares the circulation hash, the seven circulation outputs and all seventeen respiratory readout values, so this link cannot silently rot. The respiratory chain's own hash is not printed for the resting protocol by any engine command (only the perturbation arms print one), so the respiratory state is pinned by its full readout — every value the readout prints — rather than by a hash the record would have to take on trust.

presentation_stages.narrative: A 71-year-old woman presents to the emergency department twelve days after a left total knee arthroplasty with six hours of acute breathlessness and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. She has been largely chair-bound since the operation. Vitals (case data): temperature 37.4 C, heart rate 112/min, blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 26/min, SpO2 90% on room air. Examination: mild symmetric pitting oedema at both ankles; JVP not elevated; chest clear in all fields — no crackles, no wheeze, symmetric breath sounds; alert and oriented. She sleeps flat on one pillow without worsening. The learner must commit a stage-1 board before any result exists.
presentation_stages.title: History, vitals, examination

presentation_stages.narrative: First results return together. Arterial gas on room air: PaO2 62, PaCO2 30, pH 7.49, bicarbonate 22 — hypoxaemia with a wide alveolar-arterial gradient. BNP 385 pg/mL (raised). D-dimer 3,850 ug/L FEU (strongly positive against either cutoff). Troponin 34 ng/L (mildly raised). White cell count 9.6, CRP 18, urea 6.2. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ischaemic change. Chest film: clear fields, normal heart size, no effusion, no pneumothorax. And the examination battery's measurement: right calf 2.5 cm larger than the left, tender along the deep veins. The learner re-ranks — and the BNP does its work on him.
presentation_stages.title: First results: gases, biomarkers, film, leg measurement

presentation_stages.narrative: CT pulmonary angiography: occlusive filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery extending into the lobar branches, a segmental defect in the left lower lobe, and a dilated right ventricle (RV/LV 1.1). The learner's own bedside lung ultrasound, ordered to confirm the pulmonary oedema his frame predicts, shows A-lines and no B-lines in any zone. The learner re-ranks and commits.
presentation_stages.title: Definitive imaging and bedside ultrasound

presentation_stages.narrative: Adjudication and disposition. The five declared blocks are read at their final states — Wells complete at 6.0 (PE likely), PERC positive at 5 with its precondition unmet, CURB-65 at 1, the gas classified as a ventilation/perfusion mismatch, and the confirmed embolism classified intermediate-high on the ESC table. The debrief (generated by tools/case_run.py, independently recomputed by tools/case_check.py) scores the attempt's boards against this adjudication.
presentation_stages.title: Adjudication, management, disposition

case.synthetic_note: SYNTHETIC CASE. The patient is an authored fiction built for teaching; no real patient data exists in this module (design/07, master plan section 8 rule 9: education-only scope). Clinical facts the case uses — the Wells, PERC and CURB-65 instruments, the ESC severity classification, every likelihood ratio, reference range and cutoff — trace to the sources registered in cases/parameters.json (C35-C47, consulted in-session at Milestone 48), and the patient's particulars are case data, labelled as such wherever they appear.
case.title: Acute dyspnoea after knee replacement — the number that pointed at the wrong organ

validity.consequences: Scores are formative feedback only; no credentialing, progression, or clinical decision may rest on them.
validity.internal_structure: Component scores derived from the case model by stated rules (cases/parameters.json); no composite score is computed, because design/07 defines components (Brier-style calibration, anchoring, evidence quality) and no weights — inventing weights would violate the precision law. Calibration proper needs a case series; six cases now exist and are still not a calibration series — the debrief says so.
